analysis: Market regime is a confirmed uptrend (SPY +1.2% vs SMA50, 20d slope +4.91%), which opens the door to selective long exposure. The account is fully in cash with a single prior loss (ADSK -3.69%, stop hit). The honest lesson from that trade: ADSK was extended and the setup was marginal. Today I'm narrowing to three names with a clear fundamental quality advantage AND a technical basing setup in the lower half of their 52-week range. I'm deliberately avoiding: (1) names with near-term earnings within ~3 weeks (FDS earnings July 1, PAYX/CCL earnings June 24), (2) names already in the upper 80%+ of their 52-week range (APH, EOG — late-cycle extension risk), (3) names with deteriorating analyst revisions (HOOD -5.3%, RCL -3.1%, CPB -11.4%), and (4) names in MIXED/SIDEWAYS trend with declining SMA50 slope (NOW, WDAY, ECL, CTAS). The three selected — IQV, A, and ADP — each have: exceptional business quality (high ROE, strong FCF, wide margins), reasonable forward valuation, confirmed uptrend with basing characteristics in the lower half of the 52-week range, and no earnings catalyst for 40-76 days. Total deployment ~75% of equity, 25% kept in cash as dry powder. Each position is sized so a full stop-out costs ~1.5% of total equity, with no single name exceeding 25% of portfolio. Concentration is 3 positions which is within the 3-5 target. No thesis-break review needed since there are no open positions.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $180.81 or better; will accept fill up to $183. Prefer to enter on a quiet consolidation day rather than chasing a gap-up open.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: IQVIA is a dominant healthcare data, analytics, and clinical research organization with a genuine competitive moat. Fwd P/E of 12.74 and PEG of 0.74 represent exceptional value for a business growing revenue 8.4% with 22.5% ROE and $2.2B FCF. The forward P/E vs trailing P/E gap (12.74 vs 22.46) signals strong expected earnings acceleration. High D/E (255) is the main risk but is typical for this industry and is service-backed, not capital-asset-backed. Technical: Price at 30% of 52-week range (lower half ✓), confirmed uptrend with basing pattern, SMA50 slope +1.8% (rising base), only +4.6% above SMA50 (not extended), and SMA200 catchup phase underway. Next earnings July 21 (40 days away) gives enough time for position to mature before event risk.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if price closes below stop $170.23 (1.5x ATR). Exit if SMA50 slope turns negative for two consecutive weeks. Consider trimming 50% into earnings on July 21 to reduce binary risk; hold remainder if quarterly confirms thesis. Full exit if revenue growth decelerates below 5% or guidance cut materially.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $131.10 or pullback toward $129-130 (near SMA50). Do not chase above $134.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: Agilent is a high-quality life sciences instrumentation and diagnostics business. ROE 21.3%, operating margin 23.7%, FCF $931M, and 10% revenue growth represent a genuinely excellent business. Forward P/E 19.84 is reasonable for this quality tier. Conservative D/E (49.73) provides balance sheet resilience. Revenue inflection from biopharma capex recovery supports multi-quarter tailwind. Technical: At 45% of 52-week range (mid-lower half ✓), confirmed uptrend, SMA50 slope +4.1% (accelerating), price +9.4% above SMA50 (slightly extended but SMA50 itself is trending up strongly). Critically, next earnings is August 26 (76 days away) — the longest runway of any quality candidate, minimizing near-term event risk. The SMA200 crossover (+0.9%) is a positive recent development signaling Stage 2 transition.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop $123.24 (1.5x ATR below entry). Thesis break: if life sciences capex commentary from peers turns negative, or if Agilent pre-announces a revenue miss. Time stop: if price has not progressed toward $145 within 8 weeks, reassess whether base is forming or deteriorating. Consider LTCG upgrade if still holding at 11 months with intact thesis.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit at $229.91 or pullback toward $225-228 (near SMA50 support). Do not enter if gap-opens above $236.
trades.rationale: Fundamental: ADP is one of the highest-quality businesses in the S&P 500. ROE 71.2%, operating margin 30.2%, FCF $4.7B on $91.9B market cap — the FCF yield and earnings quality are exceptional. PEG 2.14 is the only modest valuation concern, but for a capital-light, recurring-revenue, economically resilient payroll/HR platform, this premium is historically justified. Analyst revisions +1.9% (positive drift). The business is effectively recession-resistant. Technical: 35% of 52-week range (lower half ✓), confirmed uptrend basing, SMA50 slope +2.8% (steady climb), +8.4% above SMA50 (slightly stretched but with low ATR of 2.8%, this is only 3 ATR units — acceptable). Low ATR means tight stop relative to target, producing excellent RR of 3.6x. Earnings July 29 (48 days out) — enough runway for the position to establish.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop $220.25. Thesis break: if payroll processing volumes decelerate materially, suggesting macro deterioration, or if a competitor wins a major enterprise contract cycle. Consider holding past 1 year for LTCG if position is profitable and thesis intact at 11 months. Trim 30% before July 29 earnings to reduce binary risk; restore size post-earnings if results confirm.
